body.prompt:
Below are the source notes of a data migration. They are authoritative. For each of the six legacy systems report:
- numeric_date_order: how NUMERIC dates in that system must be read. "DMY" = day first (05/08/2023 is 5 August), "MDY" = month first (05/08/2023 is 8 May). "none" if the notes say nothing about numeric dates for it.
- balance_sign: the master list counts a positive amount as money the counterparty owes us. "same" if the notes say the printed sign already matches the master; "opposite" if the notes say the master records the opposite sign (for example a positive printed figure is money we owe the account holder, or "is negative in the master"); "none" if the notes say nothing about the sign.
- update_dates_real: false ONLY if the notes say the system's own date stamps do not show when its data really changed (a copy, restore, re-import or migration re-stamped them). true if the notes call them real change dates or say nothing.
- void_values: the exact values of the status field that make a row void (not migrated). The field is: BRIGHTDESK = stage; LEDGR = Status; ATLAS = the trailing status tag at the end of the line; VENDEX = the closing phrase that ends an entry; KOBO = flag; VERITAS = env. List only values the notes say must NOT be migrated. Empty list if none. Values the notes say to keep are never listed.
- quote: one sentence copied character for character from the notes that supports this system's rules.

NOTES:
<<<
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). BRIGHTDESK does not use the American order for numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the same way as the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. Treat rows marked stage=hold exactly like stage=customer rows.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. LEDGR prints Saldo the opposite way to the master: positive means we owe the account holder.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Unlike the UK installation it was copied from, ATLAS writes the month first in numeric birth dates. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. A positive "owed" figure is a debt of the supplier to us; the master keeps its sign. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. The team moved from Glasgow to Milwaukee in 2015 and has written numeric dates the local way ever since. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances are receivables: positive means the member owes us. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. KOBO is not a read-only mirror: it sets upd when the data actually changes.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Do not confuse "env":"import" with production traffic: these rows are not real accounts and stay out of the master list. The ts column of VERITAS shows when the nightly copy job last rewrote the row; during the rebuild of 8 June 2025–13 July 2025 it rewrote every row, so the column no longer says when the data changed.
>>>

body.prompt:
Each entry below is one free-text record ("Vendex <id> — ..."). Return one item per entry with:
- given, family: the person's given and family name, without titles (Mr, Dr, Prof, Mrs...), without middle initials and without parentheses.
- dob: the birth date exactly as written (copy the substring). null if missing or unknown.

NOTES:
<<<
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). BRIGHTDESK does not use the American order for numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the same way as the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. Treat rows marked stage=hold exactly like stage=customer rows.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. LEDGR prints Saldo the opposite way to the master: positive means we owe the account holder.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Unlike the UK installation it was copied from, ATLAS writes the month first in numeric birth dates. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. A positive "owed" figure is a debt of the supplier to us; the master keeps its sign. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. The team moved from Glasgow to Milwaukee in 2015 and has written numeric dates the local way ever since. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances are receivables: positive means the member owes us. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. KOBO is not a read-only mirror: it sets upd when the data actually changes.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Do not confuse "env":"import" with production traffic: these rows are not real accounts and stay out of the master list. The ts column of VERITAS shows when the nightly copy job last rewrote the row; during the rebuild of 8 June 2025–13 July 2025 it rewrote every row, so the column no longer says when the data changed.
>>>

Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo changes sign in the master. Rows marked Status "Altdaten" are customers we still serve, whatever the label suggests; keep them.

Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). ATLAS formats numeric dates the way people do in the country where its servers stand, the United States. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. The "owed" column is what we owe the supplier, not what the supplier owes us, so the master records it with the opposite sign (a "CR" figure becomes positive). A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates follow the European convention, day/month/year, not the American month/day/year. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. NOTES:
<<<
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). BRIGHTDESK does not use the American order for numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances are prepaid deposits we hold for the customer, not open invoices, so the master records them with the opposite sign. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. BRIGHTDESK never re-stamps rows: its updated always shows the true date of the last change.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo changes sign in the master. Rows marked Status "Altdaten" are customers we still serve, whatever the label suggests; keep them.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). ATLAS formats numeric dates the way people do in the country where its servers stand, the United States. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. The "owed" column is what we owe the supplier, not what the supplier owes us, so the master records it with the opposite sign (a "CR" figure becomes positive). A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates follow the European convention, day/month/year, not the American month/day/year. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances keep their sign in the master. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. "flag: TRIAL" marks applications that were rejected during onboarding; do not keep these rows.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Every ts value in VERITAS falls between 17 October 2024 and 27 November 2024 because the vendor re-imported the whole table then; these dates say nothing about real changes.
>>>

The team works from Prague and writes numeric dates the way people there do. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. A positive balance is money we owe the member, so it is negative in the master. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. VERITAS was migrated to new hardware between 30 August 2024 and 24 September 2024, and the migration overwrote ts on every row with the migration date.

Below are the source notes of a data migration. They are authoritative. For each of the six legacy systems report:
- numeric_date_order: how NUMERIC dates in that system must be read. "DMY" = day first (05/08/2023 is 5 August), "MDY" = month first (05/08/2023 is 8 May). "none" if the notes say nothing about numeric dates for it.
- balance_sign: the master list counts a positive amount as money the counterparty owes us. "same" if the notes say the printed sign already matches the master; "opposite" if the notes say the master records the opposite sign (for example a positive printed figure is money we owe the account holder, or "is negative in the master"); "none" if the notes say nothing about the sign.
- update_dates_real: false ONLY if the notes say the system's own date stamps do not show when its data really changed (a copy, restore, re-import or migration re-stamped them). true if the notes call them real change dates or say nothing.
- void_values: the exact values of the status field that make a row void (not migrated). The field is: BRIGHTDESK = stage; LEDGR = Status; ATLAS = the trailing status tag at the end of the line; VENDEX = the closing phrase that ends an entry; KOBO = flag; VERITAS = env. List only values the notes say must NOT be migrated. Empty list if none. Values the notes say to keep are never listed.

NOTES:
<<<
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). BRIGHTDESK does not use the American order for numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the same way as the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. Treat rows marked stage=hold exactly like stage=customer rows.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. The team moved from Glasgow to Milwaukee in 2015 and has written numeric dates the local way ever since. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances are receivables: positive means the member owes us. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. KOBO is not a read-only mirror: it sets upd when the data actually changes.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Do not confuse "env":"import" with production traffic: these rows are not real accounts and stay out of the master list. The ts column of VERITAS shows when the nightly copy job last rewrote the row; during the rebuild of 8 June 2025–13 July 2025 it rewrote every row, so the column no longer says when the data changed.
>>>

body.prompt:
Below are the source notes of a data migration. They are authoritative. For each of the six legacy systems report:
- numeric_date_order: how NUMERIC dates in that system must be read. "DMY" = day first (05/08/2023 is 5 August), "MDY" = month first (05/08/2023 is 8 May). "none" if the notes say nothing about numeric dates for it.
- balance_sign: the master list counts a positive amount as money the counterparty owes us. "same" if the notes say the printed sign already matches the master; "opposite" if the notes say the master records the opposite sign (for example a positive printed figure is money we owe the account holder, or "is negative in the master"); "none" if the notes say nothing about the sign.
- update_dates_real: false ONLY if the notes say the system's own date stamps do not show when its data really changed (a copy, restore, re-import or migration re-stamped them). true if the notes call them real change dates or say nothing.
- void_values: the exact values of the status field that make a row void (not migrated). The field is: BRIGHTDESK = stage; LEDGR = Status; ATLAS = the trailing status tag at the end of the line; VENDEX = the closing phrase that ends an entry; KOBO = flag; VERITAS = env. List only values the notes say must NOT be migrated. Empty list if none. Values the notes say to keep are never listed.
- quote: one sentence copied character for character from the notes that supports this system's rules.

NOTES:
<<<
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). BRIGHTDESK does not use the American order for numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the same way as the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. Treat rows marked stage=hold exactly like stage=customer rows.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. LEDGR prints Saldo the opposite way to the master: positive means we owe the account holder.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Unlike the UK installation it was copied from, ATLAS writes the month first in numeric birth dates. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. A positive "owed" figure is a debt of the supplier to us; the master keeps its sign. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. The team moved from Glasgow to Milwaukee in 2015 and has written numeric dates the local way ever since. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances are receivables: positive means the member owes us. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. KOBO is not a read-only mirror: it sets upd when the data actually changes.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Do not confuse "env":"import" with production traffic: these rows are not real accounts and stay out of the master list. The ts column of VERITAS shows when the nightly copy job last rewrote the row; during the rebuild of 8 June 2025–13 July 2025 it rewrote every row, so the column no longer says when the data changed.
>>>

body.prompt:
Below are the source notes of a data migration. They are authoritative. For each of the six legacy systems report:
- numeric_date_order: how NUMERIC dates in that system must be read. "DMY" = day first (05/08/2023 is 5 August), "MDY" = month first (05/08/2023 is 8 May). "none" if the notes say nothing about numeric dates for it.
- balance_sign: the master list counts a positive amount as money the counterparty owes us. "same" if the notes say the printed sign already matches the master; "opposite" if the notes say the master records the opposite sign (for example a positive printed figure is money we owe the account holder, or "is negative in the master"); "none" if the notes say nothing about the sign.
- update_dates_real: false ONLY if the notes say the system's own date stamps do not show when its data really changed (a copy, restore, re-import or migration re-stamped them). true if the notes call them real change dates or say nothing.
- void_values: the exact values of the status field that make a row void (not migrated). The field is: BRIGHTDESK = stage; LEDGR = Status; ATLAS = the trailing status tag at the end of the line; VENDEX = the closing phrase that ends an entry; KOBO = flag; VERITAS = env. List only values the notes say must NOT be migrated. Empty list if none. Values the notes say to keep are never listed.
- quote: one sentence copied character for character from the notes that supports this system's rules.

NOTES:
<<<
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). BRIGHTDESK does not use the American order for numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances are prepaid deposits we hold for the customer, not open invoices, so the master records them with the opposite sign. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. BRIGHTDESK never re-stamps rows: its updated always shows the true date of the last change.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo changes sign in the master. Rows marked Status "Altdaten" are customers we still serve, whatever the label suggests; keep them.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). ATLAS formats numeric dates the way people do in the country where its servers stand, the United States. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. The "owed" column is what we owe the supplier, not what the supplier owes us, so the master records it with the opposite sign (a "CR" figure becomes positive). A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates follow the European convention, day/month/year, not the American month/day/year. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances keep their sign in the master. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. "flag: TRIAL" marks applications that were rejected during onboarding; do not keep these rows.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Every ts value in VERITAS falls between 17 October 2024 and 27 November 2024 because the vendor re-imported the whole table then; these dates say nothing about real changes.
>>>

body.prompt:
Below are the source notes of a data migration. They are authoritative. For each of the six legacy systems report:
- numeric_date_order: how NUMERIC dates in that system must be read. "DMY" = day first (05/08/2023 is 5 August), "MDY" = month first (05/08/2023 is 8 May). "none" if the notes say nothing about numeric dates for it.
- balance_sign: the master list counts a positive amount as money the counterparty owes us. "same" if the notes say the printed sign already matches the master; "opposite" if the notes say the master records the opposite sign (for example a positive printed figure is money we owe the account holder, or "is negative in the master"); "none" if the notes say nothing about the sign.
- update_dates_real: false ONLY if the notes say the system's own date stamps do not show when its data really changed (a copy, restore, re-import or migration re-stamped them). true if the notes call them real change dates or say nothing.
- void_values: the exact values of the status field that make a row void (not migrated). The field is: BRIGHTDESK = stage; LEDGR = Status; ATLAS = the trailing status tag at the end of the line; VENDEX = the closing phrase that ends an entry; KOBO = flag; VERITAS = env. List only values the notes say must NOT be migrated. Empty list if none. Values the notes say to keep are never listed.
- quote: one sentence copied character for character from the notes that supports this system's rules.

NOTES:
<<<
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). A customer with dob=06/02/1965 was born in June. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the opposite way to the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. BRIGHTDESK's updated is the real date of the last change; the vendor confirmed this during the 2023 audit.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. A positive Saldo is money we owe the account holder; in the master it becomes negative, and a negative Saldo becomes positive. Rows marked Status "Altdaten" are customers we still serve, whatever the label suggests; keep them. This LEDGR extract comes from a read-only mirror that was rebuilt between 25 April 2025 and 31 May 2025: the Geändert value of every LEDGR row is the time the mirror copied it, not the time the record last changed.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). An ATLAS row "born 01/08/1984" belongs to someone born in August. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. ATLAS is our accounts-payable ledger: "owed" is money we have to pay, which is a credit (negative) in the master, and a "CR" figure is money the supplier owes us. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void. Rows marked ":: QUERY" look like genuine, dormant accounts but are leftovers of an aborted import; they are void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. The team moved from Columbus to Lisbon in 2015 and has written numeric dates the local way ever since. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. The balance is the value of unpaid orders, which the member owes us; it is not store credit. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic.
>>>

"Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances change sign in the master. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. The upd value of KOBO rows is reliable: the application sets it whenever a field is edited.

Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Do not confuse "env":"replay" with production traffic: these rows are not real accounts and stay out of the master list.

body.prompt:
Below are the source notes of a data migration. They are authoritative. For each of the six legacy systems report:
- numeric_date_order: how NUMERIC dates in that system must be read. "DMY" = day first (05/08/2023 is 5 August), "MDY" = month first (05/08/2023 is 8 May). "none" if the notes say nothing about numeric dates for it.
- balance_sign: the master list counts a positive amount as money the counterparty owes us. "same" if the notes say the printed sign already matches the master; "opposite" if the notes say the master records the opposite sign (for example a positive printed figure is money we owe the account holder, or "is negative in the master"); "none" if the notes say nothing about the sign.
- update_dates_real: false ONLY if the notes say the system's own date stamps do not show when its data really changed (a copy, restore, re-import or migration re-stamped them). true if the notes call them real change dates or say nothing.
- void_values: the exact values of the status field that make a row void (not migrated). The field is: BRIGHTDESK = stage; LEDGR = Status; ATLAS = the trailing status tag at the end of the line; VENDEX = the closing phrase that ends an entry; KOBO = flag; VERITAS = env. List only values the notes say must NOT be migrated. Empty list if none. Values the notes say to keep are never listed.
- quote: one sentence copied character for character from the notes that supports this system's rules.

NOTES:
<<<
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). Although BRIGHTDESK is a US sales CRM, the instance was cloned from the London office and runs in UK locale: numeric birth dates are day/month/year. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances keep their sign in the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. Do not trust the updated dates of BRIGHTDESK: the system was restored from an old backup between 11 June 2025 and 8 July 2025, and the restore re-stamped every row.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from the account holder's side, not from ours: a positive Saldo is a credit they hold with us (negative in the master), a negative Saldo is what they owe us. LEDGR is not a read-only mirror: it sets Geändert when the data actually changes.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). For example, an ATLAS birth date written 06/02/1966 is 6 February 1966. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. The "owed" column is what we owe the supplier, not what the supplier owes us, so the master records it with the opposite sign (a "CR" figure becomes positive). A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void. Rows marked ":: QUERY" were created by a load-test tool and never belonged to a customer; they must be dropped, not migrated.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. The team never adopted the month-first habit of its American suppliers. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances change sign in the master. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void.

Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. body.prompt:
Below are the source notes of a data migration. They are authoritative. For each of the six legacy systems report:
- numeric_date_order: how NUMERIC dates in that system must be read. "DMY" = day first (05/08/2023 is 5 August), "MDY" = month first (05/08/2023 is 8 May). "none" if the notes say nothing about numeric dates for it.
- balance_sign: the master list counts a positive amount as money the counterparty owes us. "same" if the notes say the printed sign already matches the master; "opposite" if the notes say the master records the opposite sign (for example a positive printed figure is money we owe the account holder, or "is negative in the master"); "none" if the notes say nothing about the sign.
- update_dates_real: false ONLY if the notes say the system's own date stamps do not show when its data really changed (a copy, restore, re-import or migration re-stamped them). true if the notes call them real change dates or say nothing.
- void_values: the exact values of the status field that make a row void (not migrated). The field is: BRIGHTDESK = stage; LEDGR = Status; ATLAS = the trailing status tag at the end of the line; VENDEX = the closing phrase that ends an entry; KOBO = flag; VERITAS = env. List only values the notes say must NOT be migrated. Empty list if none. Values the notes say to keep are never listed.
- quote: one sentence copied character for character from the notes that supports this system's rules.

NOTES:
<<<
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). Although BRIGHTDESK is a US sales CRM, the instance was cloned from the London office and runs in UK locale: numeric birth dates are day/month/year. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances keep their sign in the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. Do not trust the updated dates of BRIGHTDESK: the system was restored from an old backup between 11 June 2025 and 8 July 2025, and the restore re-stamped every row.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from the account holder's side, not from ours: a positive Saldo is a credit they hold with us (negative in the master), a negative Saldo is what they owe us. LEDGR is not a read-only mirror: it sets Geändert when the data actually changes.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). For example, an ATLAS birth date written 06/02/1966 is 6 February 1966. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. The "owed" column is what we owe the supplier, not what the supplier owes us, so the master records it with the opposite sign (a "CR" figure becomes positive). A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void. Rows marked ":: QUERY" were created by a load-test tool and never belonged to a customer; they must be dropped, not migrated.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. The team never adopted the month-first habit of its American suppliers. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date.
