body.prompt:
Below are the source notes of a data migration. They are authoritative. For each of two legacy systems (BRIGHTDESK, VENDEX) say how NUMERIC dates in its birth dates must be read:
- "DMY" = day first (05/08/2023 is 5 August), "MDY" = month first (05/08/2023 is 8 May), "none" if the notes say nothing about numeric dates for that system.
Use the notes' own statements and examples.

NOTES:
<<<
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). BRIGHTDESK does not use the American order for numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the same way as the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. Treat rows marked stage=hold exactly like stage=customer rows.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. LEDGR prints Saldo the opposite way to the master: positive means we owe the account holder.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Unlike the UK installation it was copied from, ATLAS writes the month first in numeric birth dates. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. A positive "owed" figure is a debt of the supplier to us; the master keeps its sign. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. The team moved from Glasgow to Milwaukee in 2015 and has written numeric dates the local way ever since. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances are receivables: positive means the member owes us. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. KOBO is not a read-only mirror: it sets upd when the data actually changes.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Do not confuse "env":"import" with production traffic: these rows are not real accounts and stay out of the master list. The ts column of VERITAS shows when the nightly copy job last rewrote the row; during the rebuild of 8 June 2025–13 July 2025 it rewrote every row, so the column no longer says when the data changed.
>>>

body.prompt:
Below are the source notes of a data migration. They are authoritative. For each of the six legacy systems report:
- balance_sign: the master list counts a positive amount as money the counterparty owes us. "same" if the notes say the printed sign already matches the master; "opposite" if the notes say the master records the opposite sign (for example a positive printed figure is money we owe the account holder, or "is negative in the master"); "none" if the notes say nothing about the sign.
- update_dates_real: false ONLY if the notes say the system's own date stamps do not show when its data really changed (a copy, restore, re-import or migration re-stamped them). true if the notes call them real change dates or say nothing.
- quote: one sentence copied character for character from the notes that supports this system's rules.

NOTES:
<<<
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). BRIGHTDESK does not use the American order for numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances are prepaid deposits we hold for the customer, not open invoices, so the master records them with the opposite sign. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. BRIGHTDESK never re-stamps rows: its updated always shows the true date of the last change.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

>>>

- revised: the revision date exactly as written. For a call note ("Spoke with X on DATE") the call date is the revision date. null if none.

body.prompt:
Below are the source notes of a data migration. They are authoritative. For each of the six legacy systems report:
- balance_sign: the master list counts a positive amount as money the counterparty owes us. "same" if the notes say the printed sign already matches the master; "opposite" if the notes say the master records the opposite sign (for example a positive printed figure is money we owe the account holder, or "is negative in the master"); "none" if the notes say nothing about the sign.
- update_dates_real: false ONLY if the notes say the system's own date stamps do not show when its data really changed (a copy, restore, re-import or migration re-stamped them). true if the notes call them real change dates or say nothing.
- quote: one sentence copied character for character from the notes that supports this system's rules.

NOTES:
<<<
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). For example, dob=01/02/1996 is 2 January 1996. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. Balances are open invoices, not prepaid deposits: the customer owes us. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. Rows marked stage=review belong to customers who are still on the books; they must be migrated, not dropped.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from our side, not from the account holder's side: a positive Saldo is what the account holder owes us. Rows marked Status "inaktiv" were opened by the auditors to test the system, whatever the label suggests; leave them out.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). ATLAS is a UK ledger, but its birth dates are not day-first: the month comes first. Caution: ATLAS went live on 23 July 2007, but the date that matters is 26 August 2020, when the hosting vendor changed: rows last changed on or after 26 August 2020 swap day and month relative to the order above; earlier rows do not. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. Do not read "owed" literally: it is the amount we still have to pay the supplier, so flip its sign for the master. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. In a numeric date the first number is the day (so 08/02/2021 falls in February). A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. A positive balance is money the member still has to pay us. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. A row marked "flag: PAUSED" counts as carrying a void marker; drop it. KOBO was restored from an old backup once, in 2024, but the restore kept the original upd values, so they are real change dates.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Every ts value in VERITAS falls between 8 May 2025 and 5 June 2025 because the vendor re-imported the whole table then; these dates say nothing about real changes.
>>>

body.prompt:
Below are the source notes of a data migration. They are authoritative. For each of the six legacy systems report:
- balance_sign: the master list counts a positive amount as money the counterparty owes us. "same" if the notes say the printed sign already matches the master; "opposite" if the notes say the master records the opposite sign (for example a positive printed figure is money we owe the account holder, or "is negative in the master"); "none" if the notes say nothing about the sign.
- update_dates_real: false ONLY if the notes say the system's own date stamps do not show when its data really changed (a copy, restore, re-import or migration re-stamped them). true if the notes call them real change dates or say nothing.
- quote: one sentence copied character for character from the notes that supports this system's rules.

NOTES:
<<<
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance kept its vendor's American defaults, so the month comes before the day in numeric birth dates; the London office's day-first setup was never applied. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the same way as the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. A row marked stage=review does not carry a void marker; keep it. The updated value of BRIGHTDESK rows is reliable: the application sets it whenever a field is edited.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. A positive Saldo is money we owe the account holder; in the master it becomes negative, and a negative Saldo becomes positive.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Read numeric ATLAS birth dates as MM/DD/YYYY, never as DD/MM/YYYY. On 31 May 2023, ATLAS moved to a new hosting vendor; in rows last changed on or after that day, numeric birth dates have day and month the other way round from the order above. Earlier rows are unaffected. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. ATLAS is our accounts-payable ledger: "owed" is money we have to pay, which is a credit (negative) in the master, and a "CR" figure is money the supplier owes us. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. A numeric date such as 03/07/2021 means March 7, 2021. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. A positive balance is money the member still has to pay us. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. "flag: GUEST" marks applications that were rejected during onboarding; do not keep these rows.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Rows marked "env":"backfill" look like genuine, dormant accounts but are leftovers of an aborted import; they are void. The ts column of VERITAS shows when the nightly copy job last rewrote the row; during the rebuild of 22 June 2025–24 July 2025 it rewrote every row, so the column no longer says when the data changed.
>>>

Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance kept its vendor's American defaults, so the month comes before the day in numeric birth dates; the London office's day-first setup was never applied. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the same way as the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. A row marked stage=review does not carry a void marker; keep it. The updated value of BRIGHTDESK rows is reliable: the application sets it whenever a field is edited.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. A positive Saldo is money we owe the account holder; in the master it becomes negative, and a negative Saldo becomes positive.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. A positive balance is money the member still has to pay us. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Rows marked "env":"backfill" look like genuine, dormant accounts but are leftovers of an aborted import; they are void. The ts column of VERITAS shows when the nightly copy job last rewrote the row; during the rebuild of 22 June 2025–24 July 2025 it rewrote every row, so the column no longer says when the data changed.
>>>

Each entry below is one free-text record ("Vendex <id> — ..."). Return one item per entry with:
- given, family: the person's given and family name, without titles (Mr, Dr, Prof, Mrs...), without middle initials and without parentheses.

- revised: the revision date exactly as written. For a call note ("Spoke with X on DATE") the call date is the revision date. null if none.
- phone: the phone number exactly as written (copy the substring). null if none.
- country: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the country the supplier is in, when the entry states it or implies it (a nationality adjective such as "a Dutch supplier", or a city such as "based in Mannheim"). null if the location is not stated.
- amount: the balance figure exactly as written, including its currency word or code (for example "thirty-two euros and twenty-nine cents" or "EUR 825.91"). null if the entry records no balance ("no balance recorded", "balance not recorded").
- currency: ISO 4217 code of that balance ("dollars" = USD, "euros" = EUR, "pounds" = GBP). null when amount is null.
- direction: "credit_to_customer" if the entry says the supplier holds a credit or that we owe them; otherwise "owed_to_us" (balance due, owes us, outstanding, open balance).

body.prompt:
Below are the source notes of a data migration. They are authoritative. For each of the six legacy systems report:
- balance_sign: the master list counts a positive amount as money the counterparty owes us. "same" if the notes say the printed sign already matches the master; "opposite" if the notes say the master records the opposite sign (for example a positive printed figure is money we owe the account holder, or "is negative in the master"); "none" if the notes say nothing about the sign.
- update_dates_real: false ONLY if the notes say the system's own date stamps do not show when its data really changed (a copy, restore, re-import or migration re-stamped them). true if the notes call them real change dates or say nothing.
- quote: one sentence copied character for character from the notes that supports this system's rules.

NOTES:
<<<
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). The instance kept its vendor's American defaults, so the month comes before the day in numeric birth dates; the London office's day-first setup was never applied. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. A positive balance is money the customer still has to pay us; a credit is money we owe the customer. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. Rows marked stage=legacy are customers we still serve, whatever the label suggests; keep them. Every updated value in BRIGHTDESK falls between 7 November 2024 and 21 December 2024 because the vendor re-imported the whole table then; these dates say nothing about real changes.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from our side, not from the account holder's side: a positive Saldo is what the account holder owes us.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). An ATLAS row "born 08/01/1950" belongs to someone born in August. Caution: ATLAS went live on 12 April 2008, but the date that matters is 27 October 2021, when the hosting vendor changed: rows last changed on or after 27 October 2021 swap day and month relative to the order above; earlier rows do not. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. A positive "owed" figure is a debt of ours to the supplier; the master stores it as a negative balance. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void. A row marked ":: ARCHIVE" counts as carrying a void marker; drop it.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates are MM/DD/YYYY. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. The balance is the value of unpaid orders, which the member owes us; it is not store credit. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. Nobody ever bought anything through a row marked "flag: GUEST", so it is void. KOBO's upd is the real date of the last change; the vendor confirmed this during the 2019 audit.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic.
>>>

- given, family: the person's given and family name, without titles (Mr, Dr, Prof, Mrs...), without middle initials and without parentheses.
- dob: the birth date exactly as written (copy the substring). null if missing or unknown.
- revised: the revision date exactly as written. For a call note ("Spoke with X on DATE") the call date is the revision date. null if none.
- phone: the phone number exactly as written (copy the substring). null if none.
- country: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the country the supplier is in, when the entry states it or implies it (a nationality adjective such as "a Dutch supplier", or a city such as "based in Mannheim"). null if the location is not stated.
- amount: the balance figure exactly as written, including its currency word or code (for example "thirty-two euros and twenty-nine cents" or "EUR 825.91"). null if the entry records no balance ("no balance recorded", "balance not recorded").

- direction: "credit_to_customer" if the entry says the supplier holds a credit or that we owe them; otherwise "owed_to_us" (balance due, owes us, outstanding, open balance).

body.prompt:
Below are the source notes of a data migration. They are authoritative. For each of the six legacy systems report:
- balance_sign: the master list counts a positive amount as money the counterparty owes us. "same" if the notes say the printed sign already matches the master; "opposite" if the notes say the master records the opposite sign (for example a positive printed figure is money we owe the account holder, or "is negative in the master"); "none" if the notes say nothing about the sign.
- update_dates_real: false ONLY if the notes say the system's own date stamps do not show when its data really changed (a copy, restore, re-import or migration re-stamped them). true if the notes call them real change dates or say nothing.
- quote: one sentence copied character for character from the notes that supports this system's rules.

NOTES:
<<<
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). BRIGHTDESK does not use the American order for numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the opposite way to the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. BRIGHTDESK was restored from an old backup once, in 2019, but the restore kept the original updated values, so they are real change dates.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from the account holder's side, not from ours: a positive Saldo is a credit they hold with us (negative in the master), a negative Saldo is what they owe us. Do not confuse Status "inaktiv" with "storniert" entries: these rows are real accounts and stay in the master list.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). An ATLAS row "born 03/11/1966" belongs to someone born in November. Caution: ATLAS went live on 27 December 2008, but the date that matters is 23 June 2020, when the hosting vendor changed: rows last changed on or after 23 June 2020 swap day and month relative to the order above; earlier rows do not. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. The "owed" column is what we owe the supplier, not what the supplier owes us, so the master records it with the opposite sign (a "CR" figure becomes positive). A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. A numeric date such as 02/07/2021 means February 7, 2021. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances are payables: positive means we owe the member. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. Rows marked "flag: PAUSED" were created by a load-test tool and never belonged to a customer; they must be dropped, not migrated.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. Rows marked "env":"replay" look like test data but are genuine, merely dormant accounts; they are not void. The ts column of VERITAS shows when the nightly copy job last rewrote the row; during the rebuild of 7 October 2024–20 November 2024 it rewrote every row, so the column no longer says when the data changed.
>>>

body.prompt:
Below are the source notes of a data migration. They are authoritative. For each of the six legacy systems report:
- balance_sign: the master list counts a positive amount as money the counterparty owes us. "same" if the notes say the printed sign already matches the master; "opposite" if the notes say the master records the opposite sign (for example a positive printed figure is money we owe the account holder, or "is negative in the master"); "none" if the notes say nothing about the sign.
- update_dates_real: false ONLY if the notes say the system's own date stamps do not show when its data really changed (a copy, restore, re-import or migration re-stamped them). true if the notes call them real change dates or say nothing.
- quote: one sentence copied character for character from the notes that supports this system's rules.

NOTES:
<<<
SOURCE NOTES — legacy systems in this export

The export merges 6 systems: BRIGHTDESK (US sales CRM), LEDGR (German ERP for customers and suppliers across Europe and beyond), ATLAS (UK supplier ledger), VENDEX (procurement team's free-text contact register), KOBO (Japanese web shop), VERITAS (identity-verification service for KYC checks). Every line starts with its system name and row id; row ids are unique across the whole export. These notes were written by the system owners and are authoritative for reading the data.

General: a blank field means the value is missing. So do the placeholders "n/a", "—", "TBD", "?", "00/00/0000", "00.00.0000", "----/--/--" and all-zero phone numbers. Phone numbers written without an international prefix ("+", "00" or, in BRIGHTDESK only, "011") are local numbers of the row's own country.

BRIGHTDESK. Lines look like "BRIGHTDESK row=<id> | name=... | dob=... | country=... | phone=... | balance=... | updated=YYYY-MM-DD", sometimes followed by "| memo=...". Birth dates are written numerically (zero padding is inconsistent) or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985"). BRIGHTDESK does not use the American order for numeric birth dates. Names are written either "Given FAMILY" (family name in capital letters; a title may precede the given name and a middle initial may follow it) or "Family, Given" (a middle initial may follow). Balances are in US dollars; a balance in parentheses, or with a leading minus, is negative. BRIGHTDESK prints balances the opposite way to the master. Some reps typed 011, the US international access code, in front of the country code of foreign numbers. Some rows also carry a "stage" field; "stage=customer" is an ordinary live account. QA fixtures are void: a row whose name begins with "ZZTEST" must not be migrated. Rows marked stage=migrated are customers we still serve, whatever the label suggests; keep them. Do not trust the updated dates of BRIGHTDESK: the system was restored from an old backup between 24 April 2025 and 26 May 2025, and the restore re-stamped every row.

LEDGR. Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from our side, not from the account holder's side: a positive Saldo is what the account holder owes us.

Numeric dates follow the European convention, day/month/year, not the American month/day/year. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. A row marked "flag: GIFT" counts as carrying a void marker; drop it.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. The ts value of VERITAS rows is reliable: the application sets it whenever a field is edited.

Semicolon-separated positional fields: LEDGR; Satz-Nr (row id); Name as "Nachname, Vorname" (family name, given name); Anrede (salutation and academic title, may be empty); Geburtsdatum (birth date, day.month.year); Land (country, written in German); Telefon; Saldo (balance, German number format: "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal separator; currency EUR, or CHF for Swiss accounts); Status; Geändert (date of last change, day.month.year). Status "aktiv" is a live account, "gesperrt" is a blocked but real account that must still be migrated; "storniert" marks a cancelled entry, which is void. A minus sign after the number ("250,00- EUR") or before it marks a negative Saldo. Saldo is shown from our side, not from the account holder's side: a positive Saldo is what the account holder owes us.

ATLAS. Lines look like "ATLAS #<id> :: <name> :: born <birth date> :: <country> :: tel <phone> :: owed <amount in GBP> :: last change <date>", optionally with ":: note: ..." and a trailing status tag (":: <TAG>"). Names are "FAMILY, Given (Title)" or "Title Given Family". Birth dates are written numerically or, when the day is above 12, with an abbreviated month name ("25 Mar 1985" or "25-Mar-1985"). Unlike the US installation it was copied from, ATLAS writes the day first in numeric birth dates. Caution: ATLAS went live on 16 September 2004, but the date that matters is 2 October 2021, when the hosting vendor changed: rows last changed on or after 2 October 2021 swap day and month relative to the order above; earlier rows do not. Unknown birth dates appear as "n/k" or "?". "CR" after an amount marks a negative "owed" figure. A positive "owed" figure is a debt of ours to the supplier; the master stores it as a negative balance. A line ending ":: DO NOT MIGRATE" is void. Rows marked ":: DORMANT" look like genuine, dormant accounts but are leftovers of an aborted import; they are void.

VENDEX. Free-text English entries ("Vendex <id> — ...") written by the procurement team; the phrasing varies from entry to entry. Names are written given name first (with an optional title and middle initial). Dates — birth dates and the date the entry was revised — are written out in words or, when the day is 12 or less, sometimes numerically. Numeric dates follow the European convention, day/month/year, not the American month/day/year. A two-digit year in a birth date means 19xx. For a call note ("Spoke with <name> on <date>") the call date is the revision date. Balances may be written in words: "dollars" are US dollars, "euros" EUR and "pounds" GBP (pence are hundredths of a pound). "Owes us", "open balance", "outstanding" and "balance due" introduce what the supplier owes us; "in credit by", "holding a credit of", "credit balance of" and "we owe them" introduce a credit, that is a negative balance. The country is named, implied by a nationality adjective ("a Dutch supplier" is in the Netherlands), or implied by the city the supplier is based in. An entry that ends with "(Application withdrawn — never onboarded.)" is void.

KOBO. Lines look like "KOBO/<id> member: <name> | birth: <date> | tel: <phone> | balance: <yen> | upd: YYYY/MM/DD", optionally with "| note: ...". KOBO serves customers resident in Japan only, so its rows have no country field (the country is Japan) and its phone numbers are Japanese local numbers. Names are written family name first without a comma ("TANAKA Hiroshi" or "Tanaka Hiroshi"); KOBO cannot store accented letters. Birth dates are year/month/day or Japanese era notation: "S" is Shōwa (S1 = 1926, so S62 = 1987; Shōwa ended on 7 January 1989) and "H" is Heisei (H1 = 1989, starting 8 January 1989); for example H3.11.20 is 1991-11-20. Balances are in yen ("¥" or "円"); "▲" in front of an amount marks it negative, as does a minus sign. KOBO balances change sign in the master. A row with "flag: SAMPLE" is a demo account and void. A row marked "flag: GIFT" counts as carrying a void marker; drop it.

VERITAS. Each line is "VERITAS " followed by a JSON object: row, family, given, dob (ISO date), country (ISO alpha-2, except that the United Kingdom is sometimes written "UK"; letter case varies), msisdn (the full international number including country code, without "+"), amount and ccy (ISO currency code), ts (time of last update, ISO 8601 UTC) and an optional note. A dob of 1900-01-01 is the vendor's sentinel for "unknown" and is not a real birth date. Rows containing "env":"sandbox" are test traffic and void. "env":"production" marks live traffic. The ts value of VERITAS rows is reliable: the application sets it whenever a field is edited.
>>>

body.prompt:
Each entry below is one free-text record ("Vendex <id> — ..."). Return one item per entry with:
- given, family: the person's given and family name, without titles (Mr, Dr, Prof, Mrs...), without middle initials and without parentheses.
- dob: the birth date exactly as written (copy the substring). null if missing or unknown.
- revised: the revision date exactly as written. For a call note ("Spoke with X on DATE") the call date is the revision date. null if none.
- phone: the phone number exactly as written (copy the substring). null if none.
- country: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the country the supplier is in, when the entry states it or implies it (a nationality adjective such as "a Dutch supplier", or a city such as "based in Mannheim"). null if the location is not stated.
- amount: the balance figure exactly as written, including its currency word or code (for example "thirty-two euros and twenty-nine cents" or "EUR 825.91"). null if the entry records no balance ("no balance recorded", "balance not recorded").
- currency: ISO 4217 code of that balance ("dollars" = USD, "euros" = EUR, "pounds" = GBP). null when amount is null.
- direction: "credit_to_customer" if the entry says the supplier holds a credit or that we owe them; otherwise "owed_to_us" (balance due, owes us, outstanding, open balance).
